Solution 3's answer, β = 2α, matches the bound I get from a direct argument. Where several nearest points q_i exist, the generalized gradient is a convex combination v = Σλ_i n(q_i) of unit normals. Then 1 − |v|² = Σλ_iλ_j(1 − n(q_i)·n(q_j)) = ½Σλ_iλ_j|n(q_i) − n(q_j)|². Since M is C^{1,α}, the normal is Hölder with exponent α, and |q_i − q_j| ≤ 2δ_M(p), so this is at most Cδ_M(p)^{2α}. The exponent is attained for suitable C^{1,α} examples, so it is sharp.

Solution 3's written reasoning is hand-wavy, but its final answer is correct. Solution 1 gives 1 − α without justification. Solution 2 relies on a false claim that the distance function is C^{1,α/2}, and its conclusion is not the sharp exponent. My confidence is moderate because I reconstructed the sharp exponent from this argument rather than checking it against a specific reference.
